containment_sequence: preserve the immutable release package, manifest, live audit, and incident receipt
treat the checked-out repository commit as canonical and the drifting live surface as unverified
hold public-release promotion and do not cite mismatched live bytes as current evidence
separate static release drift from gateway, secret, DNS, buyer-data, and legal incident lanes
escalate any suspected SEV-1 condition for human classification without inferring it from a public HTTP audit
human_authorization_required: repair or restart the public gateway
install, rotate, or revoke a credential or secret
change DNS, firewall, TLS, reverse-proxy, or hosting configuration
notify a customer, regulator, insurer, partner, or the public
delete or disclose data or evidence
accept legal terms or make a certification or attestation
place a trade or enable production execution
close an incident after a live production change

planning_targets.buyer_data_rto_rpo: not established; must be negotiated in the signed buyer scope
planning_targets.release_byte_rpo: zero for immutable Git-tracked allowlisted release bytes

recovery_sequence: review the exact commit, manifest, affected surfaces, and rollback boundary
obtain the literal exact-snapshot deployment approval before mutating public files
obtain the separate gateway-repair approval before changing gateway dependencies or runtime secrets
apply only the allowlisted release with rollback capture
rerun the full-manifest exact-byte and MIME audit against the deployed commit
verify critical routes and retain deployment, rollback, and live-audit receipts
close only after the current commit reports release_verified true and any separate incident lane is resolved
